title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 59-60
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 59 to 60 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'वेधाः स्वाङ्गोऽजितः कृष्णो दृढः सङ्कर्षणोऽच्युतः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 59 to 60 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 59 to 60.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 59 to 60** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **वेधाः स्वाङ्गोऽजितः कृष्णो दृढः सङ्कर्षणोऽच्युतः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**वेधाः स्वाङ्गोऽजितः कृष्णो दृढः सङ्कर्षणोऽच्युतः । वरुणो वारुणो वृक्षः पुष्कराक्षो महामनाः ॥** **भगवान् भगहानन्दी वनमाली हलायुधः । आदित्यो ज्योतिरादित्यः सहिष्णुर्गतिसत्तमः ॥**

The maker, fair of limb, never defeated, Krishna is he. Firm, Sankarshana, who never slips, is that God of gods. Varuna, the tree, lotus-eyed and great of mind. He is Bhagavan, the giver of fortune, full of joy. The one with the garland of wild flowers and the plough as his weapon is that God of gods. The Sun, the light, patient, and the highest destination.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 59 to 60 mean?
faq.a: The maker, fair of limb, never defeated, Krishna is he. Firm, Sankarshana, who never slips, is that God of gods. Varuna, the tree, lotus-eyed and great of mind. He is Bhagavan, the giver of fortune, full of joy. The one with the garland of wild flowers and the plough as his weapon is that God of gods. The Sun, the light, patient, and the highest destination.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
